title: Glueing morphisms and sheaves of modules along an open covering
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$. For an open $U\subseteq X$ put $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ (the sheaf of rings $W\mapsto\mathcal O_X(W)$ on the opens $W\subseteq U$); for opens $V\subseteq U$ and a sheaf of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $\mathcal M$ on $U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal M|_V$ be the $\mathcal O_V$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal M(W)$ ($W\subseteq V$ open) with the restriction maps and module structures of $\mathcal M$, and for an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ let $\alpha|_V:\mathcal M|_V\to\mathcal N|_V$ be the $\mathcal O_V$-linear map with components $(\alpha|_V)_W=\alpha_W$ ($W\subseteq V$ open). Let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering, $U_{ij}=U_i\cap U_j$ and $U_{ijk}=U_i\cap U_j\cap U_k$. (1) (Glueing morphisms.) Let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\varphi_i:\mathcal F|_{U_i}\to\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ ($i\in I$) $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-linear maps with $\varphi_i|_{U_{ij}}=\varphi_j|_{U_{ij}}$ for all $i,j\in I$. Then there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ with $\varphi|_{U_i}=\varphi_i$ for all $i\in I$. In particular two $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ whose restrictions to every $U_i$ agree are equal. (2) (Glueing sheaves.) For each $i\in I$ let $\mathcal F_i$ be an $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-module, and for each pair $(i,j)\in I\times I$ (including $i=j$) let $\varphi_{ij}:\mathcal F_i|_{U_{ij}}\to\mathcal F_j|_{U_{ij}}$ be an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{U_{ij}}$-modules such that $\varphi_{ik}|_{U_{ijk}}=\varphi_{jk}|_{U_{ijk}}\circ\varphi_{ij}|_{U_{ijk}}$ for all $i,j,k\in I$ (cocycle condition). Then there are an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\varphi_i:\mathcal F|_{U_i}\to\mathcal F_i$ ($i\in I$) such that $\varphi_{ij}\circ\varphi_i|_{U_{ij}}=\varphi_j|_{U_{ij}}$ for all $i,j\in I$.

proof.text: *Step 1 ((1): the components of $\varphi$).* Following 04TN. Let $U\subseteq X$ be open and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. For $i\in I$ put $t_i=(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}(s|_{U\cap U_i})\in\mathcal G(U\cap U_i)$. These agree on overlaps: by naturality of $\varphi_i$ and $\varphi_j$ and the hypothesis $\varphi_i|_{U_{ij}}=\varphi_j|_{U_{ij}}$ (equality of components at the open $U\cap U_{ij}\subseteq U_{ij}$), $t_i|_{U\cap U_{ij}}=(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_{ij}}(s|_{U\cap U_{ij}})=(\varphi_j)_{U\cap U_{ij}}(s|_{U\cap U_{ij}})=t_j|_{U\cap U_{ij}}$. Since $U=\bigcup_i(U\cap U_i)$ is an open covering and $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf (of abelian groups, hence its sections glue uniquely along open coverings) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], there is a unique $\varphi_U(s)\in\mathcal G(U)$ with $\varphi_U(s)|_{U\cap U_i}=t_i$ for all $i$. This defines maps of sets $\varphi_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$ for every open $U$.

proof.text: *Step 2 ((1): $\varphi$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism).* Every identity below is checked after restriction to the opens of an open covering, which suffices because sections of the sheaf $\mathcal G$ are determined by their restrictions to the members of an open covering [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. (a) Compatibility with restriction (04TN): for opens $V\subseteq U$ and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, for every $i$, $(\varphi_U(s)|_V)|_{V\cap U_i}=(\varphi_U(s)|_{U\cap U_i})|_{V\cap U_i}=(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}(s|_{U\cap U_i})|_{V\cap U_i}=(\varphi_i)_{V\cap U_i}(s|_{V\cap U_i})=\varphi_V(s|_V)|_{V\cap U_i}$ (naturality of $\varphi_i$, then Step 1 for $V$); hence $\varphi_U(s)|_V=\varphi_V(s|_V)$ on the covering $V=\bigcup_i(V\cap U_i)$. (b) Linearity (the check on the $U_i$): for $a\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $s,s'\in\mathcal F(U)$, the restrictions of $\varphi_U(as+s')$ and of $a\varphi_U(s)+\varphi_U(s')$ to $U\cap U_i$ are $(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}(a|_{U\cap U_i}s|_{U\cap U_i}+s'|_{U\cap U_i})$ and $a|_{U\cap U_i}(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}(s|_{U\cap U_i})+(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}(s'|_{U\cap U_i})$, using that the restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are additive and semilinear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; they are equal since $(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}$ is $\mathcal O_X(U\cap U_i)$-linear. So $\varphi_U(as+s')=a\varphi_U(s)+\varphi_U(s')$. By (a) and (b), $\varphi=(\varphi_U)_U$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: *Step 3 ((1): $\varphi|_{U_i}=\varphi_i$ and uniqueness).* Following 04TN. For an open $W\subseteq U_i$ and $s\in\mathcal F(W)$ we have $W\cap U_i=W$, so Step 1 gives $\varphi_W(s)=\varphi_W(s)|_{W\cap U_i}=(\varphi_i)_W(s)$; thus $(\varphi|_{U_i})_W=(\varphi_i)_W$ for every open $W\subseteq U_i$, i.e. $\varphi|_{U_i}=\varphi_i$. If $\psi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear with $\psi|_{U_i}=\varphi_i$ for all $i$, then for every open $U$ and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $\psi_U(s)|_{U\cap U_i}=\psi_{U\cap U_i}(s|_{U\cap U_i})=(\varphi_i)_{U\cap U_i}(s|_{U\cap U_i})=t_i$, so $\psi_U(s)=\varphi_U(s)$ by the uniqueness in Step 1; hence $\psi=\varphi$ (a morphism is determined by its components [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). For the last sentence of (1): if $\alpha,\beta:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ are $\mathcal O_X$-linear with $\alpha|_{U_i}=\beta|_{U_i}$ for all $i$, the family $\varphi_i=\alpha|_{U_i}$ satisfies $\varphi_i|_{U_{ij}}=\alpha|_{U_{ij}}=\varphi_j|_{U_{ij}}$ (both have components $\alpha_W$, $W\subseteq U_{ij}$), and $\alpha$, $\beta$ both restrict to it, so $\alpha=\beta$ by the uniqueness just proved.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Sheaves Section 00AK: 04TN (lemma-glue-maps) with its proof, 00AL (lemma-glue-sheaves) with its first proof, 00AM (lemma-glue-sheaves-structures) with its proof; tags checked in tags/tags. Statement kept in substance; made self-contained: the ringed space is introduced as X with a sheaf of commutative rings, the restriction of modules and of morphisms to opens is now defined in the statement (it was attributed to def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, which does not define it), and the pairs (i,j) of (2) are said to include i=j, as Stacks' glueing data does (needed for phi_ii = id, used by the citer lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-presentation-extension, which glues with identities). Proof in 7 steps following the sources: (1) per 04TN, sections phi_U(s) glued from (phi_i)(s|) by the sheaf condition of G, compatibility with restrictions and additivity/O-linearity checked on the U_i (Step 2), restriction to U_i and uniqueness, plus the 'in particular' clause used by the citers; (2) per 00AL first proof and 00AM: F(W) the equalizer submodule of prod F_i(W cap U_i), sheaf condition from that of the F_i, phi_i the projection, bijective by the cocycle condition and phi_ii = id, compatibility square. Every step uses only the definition of sheaves of modules (the sources use only sheaf axioms). No new node; no existing node states 04TN/00AL for sets or abelian groups (lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis is the basis version, lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-on-basis-extends of unit sk-thm-reduction the basis extension used by 00AL's second proof; neither needed). Checked the four citers: grothendieck-existence-easy (steps 7-8), module-finite-presentation-representatives (steps 2, 4), module-finite-presentation-extension (step 9) and sheaf-isomorphism-local-open-cover (steps 4-5) use (1) with its uniqueness clause and (2) exactly as stated.
